findings.title: Backup is visible before it is complete
findings.description: create_backup reserves the final timestamp directory before copying, then copies into a sibling .tmp directory and moves entries one by one. During that window, list_backups treats the empty final directory, and any stale .tmp-* directory, as a valid backup because it accepts every directory under the save backup folder. A concurrent UI refresh or restore can expose/restore an empty or partial backup, and a process kill can leave bogus backups permanently listed.
findings.suggestion: Copy into a hidden temporary directory that list_backups explicitly ignores, then publish the backup with a single final rename. Also filter list_backups to timestamp-shaped directories and skip dot-prefixed temp directories.

findings.title: Restore cleanup misses shutil.Error failures
findings.description: restore_backup only catches OSError, but shutil.copytree can raise shutil.Error for aggregated copy failures. In that case temp_target is not removed, previous_target rollback is skipped if the failure happens after renaming, and callers receive an uncategorized exception instead of BackupError.
findings.suggestion: Catch Exception or at least (OSError, shutil.Error), perform the same cleanup/rollback path, then wrap the original failure in BackupError.

findings.title: Backup rename does not normalize the new name
findings.description: rename_save strips new_name before renaming the live save, and preflight_rename validates a stripped name, but rename_backups_for_save validates and uses the raw new_save_name. A quoted CLI/API rename such as '  Clean  ' moves the save to 'Clean' while moving backups to a different directory named with spaces, splitting the backup history from the save.
findings.suggestion: Normalize new_save_name once with strip() inside rename_backups_for_save and use the normalized value for validation and new_dir. Add an integration test that renames a save with backups and surrounding whitespace.

findings.title: Unknown player state renders as alive
findings.description: _save_info omits player_dead/player_x/player_y when metadata is unavailable. In Jinja, a missing dict key is Undefined, not None, so the template's 'is none' checks fail: saves without players.db render as Alive and show a blank Position '(, )'. This misreports save state in the main UI.
findings.suggestion: Initialize expected optional fields in info, for example player_dead=None, player_x=None, player_y=None, player=None, before merging extracted metadata, or use Jinja defined checks.

findings.title: Watcher backs up by default roots instead of watched path
findings.description: SaveWatcher stores a SaveGame with an explicit path, but _do_backup calls create_backup only with game_mode and name. create_backup re-resolves the save from the default saves root, so a watcher created for an overridden/custom save root can fail or, worse, back up a different default-root save with the same mode/name.
findings.suggestion: Make SaveWatcher carry saves_root/backups_root or add a backup function that copies directly from self.save.path. Ensure automatic backups use the exact watched SaveGame path.

findings.title: Per-save watcher ignores configured cooldown
findings.description: The single-save Watch button calls manager.watch(save) with default debounce/cooldown values. That bypasses backup_cooldown_minutes from config, while the all-saves watcher toggle uses the configured cooldown. Users get different auto-backup behavior depending on which UI control they used.
findings.suggestion: Read config_get_all() in api_watcher_save and pass the same configured debounce_seconds and backup_cooldown_seconds used by the bulk watcher path.

findings.title: Existing watcher settings never update
findings.description: WatcherManager.watch immediately returns an existing watcher without applying new debounce or cooldown values. After changing settings, stopping/starting the watcher, or using the bulk toggle, previously watched saves keep stale timing values.
findings.suggestion: When a watcher already exists, update its debounce_seconds and backup_cooldown_seconds or recreate/reschedule it with the requested settings.

findings.title: GUI command ignores global directory overrides
findings.description: The Click group accepts --saves-dir and --backups-dir, but gui_command does not receive ctx and run_gui has no way to consume ctx.obj. Running 'pz-saves --saves-dir X --backups-dir Y gui' launches the GUI against default/configured directories instead of the requested paths.
findings.suggestion: Add @click.pass_context to gui_command and propagate ctx.obj roots into the GUI layer, or reject those global options for the gui command if unsupported.

findings.title: Installer shortcuts point at the wrong launcher location
findings.description: PROJECT_DIR is computed as Path(__file__).parent.parent, which is the src directory in this src-layout project or site-packages when installed. install_linux and install_windows then point shortcuts at PROJECT_DIR/launcher.sh or launcher.bat, but those files are not part of the shown package location, so install can create broken launchers.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the actual installed console entry point or package a launcher resource explicitly. Validate the target exists before writing shortcuts and raise a clear error if it does not.

findings.title: count_players can raise despite defensive extractor contract
findings.description: count_players calls path.stat() outside the try block after checking is_file(). If players.db is deleted or becomes inaccessible between those calls, FileNotFoundError/OSError escapes, contradicting the module contract that extractors return None/defaults on failure.
findings.suggestion: Move both is_file() and stat() into the try block, or catch OSError around the whole existence/size check.

findings.title: Invalid CLI config values are not converted to ClickException
findings.description: config_command converts numeric values with float()/int() outside any error handling. Invalid input such as 'pz-saves config port abc' raises ValueError directly instead of producing the same clean ClickException behavior used by backup/restore commands.
findings.suggestion: Wrap config value conversion in try/except (ValueError, TypeError) and raise click.ClickException with a concise validation message.

overall_assessment: The core functionality is close, but several production-facing edge cases remain around backup publication, restore rollback, rename normalization, watcher configuration, and GUI metadata defaults. The tests cover many prior P0 cases but miss combined workflows such as whitespace rename with backups, custom roots with watchers/GUI, and incomplete temp backup visibility.
summary: 11 findings: 7 bugs, 2 error-handling issues, 1 edge case, and 1 installer quality/runtime issue.
